method.grader: evaluation.eval_detector.grade_elements — the SAME grader, matcher and goldens as every other detector number in this paper

KY.precision_reading: quality figure -- golden is detection-exhaustive over this window

findings.1_nothing_is_lost_at_scale: 0 golden elements absent in either state; 0 hallucination candidates. Recall by level and title is 1.000 in both, across a 6.5x (KY) and 4.1x (CO) page increase and 4 detection batches.
findings.2_precision_drops_at_scale_from_survivin: KY's 55 in-window detections are 44 distinct elements + 11 duplicate copies, so precision is 44/55 = 0.800 and the whole shortfall is duplication. Every duplicate is one element emitted twice on one page, once banded and once null. _dedup_elements did not merge them because the copies disagree on age_band. CO — no age-band column — shows 0 duplicates in the same measurement, which is what makes the attribution to age_band rather than to chunking credible.
findings.3_age_band_attribution_is_unstable_three: In KY's window: 20 elements banded-only (the entire strict-recall shortfall), 11 emitted twice (finding 2), 13 null-only. 5 of 7 content pages emit BOTH values. Document-wide 152/329 banded; the subset run emitted null for all 44. VERDICT OPEN — golden, run, or schema.
findings.4_KY_golden_is_vindicated: All 11 KY unmatched detections are duplicates of elements the golden already covers; 0 are unannotated content. The golden accounts for every DISTINCT element the larger run finds on its pages, at 4 batches as at 1. Two independent scans on 2026-09-06 confirm the subset golden has no missing test cases at all: the union of all 13 KY detection files contains no (level, title) it lacks, and no block of text on subset pages 2-8 is unaccounted for by one of its titles or descriptions at >=0.9 word coverage.
findings.5_CO_recall_only: CO gives 0 absent / 0 duplicates / 0 hallucinations across 4 detection batches on the corpus's hardest layout — that is its whole contribution, and it is the recall half only. Its 7-element spot-check golden leaves 55 of 61 in-window detections unannotated (none duplicates, none ungrounded), so its precision is a coverage artifact and is labelled as one in the output. DO NOT report CO precision and do not describe CO as exhaustive.
findings.6_chain_closes_at_fabricated_primary_key: KY's trimmed run produces 214 standards with 214 distinct standard_ids, of which 7 are DUPLICATES — pairs sharing parents and indicator name, separated only by disambiguate_colliding_standards' numeric `.N` fallback (US-KY-2021-AL.2.1.FNWUF beside ...FNWUF.2, same page, same parents, same name). 'Distinct' is not 'collision-free': grade_parser.id_collisions runs AFTER the resolver, so it reports zero by construction. Chain: detector emits the element twice (banded + null) -> _dedup_elements cannot merge (its key includes age_band) -> parser canonicalizes both bands to the document's single band -> identical -> collide -> `.2` reaches persistence. CO has 0 duplicates in 240 standards and no age-band column, which is the control.

traps_avoided.domain_tagging_before_filtering: Otherwise domain-scoped precision discards real false positives as out-of-scope.
traps_avoided.layout_robust_grounding: Contiguous-substring grounding reported 39 nonexistent hallucinations on CO, purely because extraction interleaves multi-column reading order. Grounding is exact-substring OR >=0.9 distinct-word coverage.
traps_avoided.page_tolerance_reported_at_0_and_1: Recall conclusions identical at both. Grounding is meaningless at tolerance 1 (it admits pages the subset PDF never held) — read tolerance 1 for recall only.
traps_avoided.duplicate_check_keyed_more_loosely_than_: The one that actually bit. See ⚠️_CORRECTION_20260906.

⚠️_CORRECTION_20260906: The first recording of this task reported 0 duplicates surviving the merge and read KY's 11 unmatched detections as an annotation gap. BOTH ARE WITHDRAWN. duplicate_analysis was keyed on eval_detector._match_key, which ends in age_band — the field the duplicates differ in — so all eleven were hidden, in the direction that flatters the system. Corrected: 11 duplicates survive the merge on KY, they are the entire precision shortfall, and KY's golden does NOT under-annotate. Generalizable lesson, now in duplicate_analysis's docstring: a duplicate check must be keyed more loosely than the merge it audits, or it can only confirm that merge's opinion of itself.

age_band_verdict.meaning: The run over-attributes the page banner onto individual elements. The golden is right and does not change. Reported as a detector defect at scale (paper §8).
age_band_verdict.no_code_change: code_version_hash stays at 14374dba; no recorded result is invalidated.
rationale: KY's expected_depth_map already describes the 'THREE AND FOUR YEAR OLDS' banner as page furniture the domain heading sits above — context, not a property.

The band already has a home one stage later: ground_truth_parser/KY.json sets default_age_band 36-60 and parse_hierarchy applies it document-wide. The detector stamping the banner on elements is a second, competing mechanism for the same fact.

All six goldens draw the same line: a detector age_band comes from a side-by-side COLUMN that distinguishes siblings (CA Early/Later, TX PK3/PK4). KY, CO, NV, AZ annotate null throughout. A banner applying to every element carries no distinguishing information.
age_band_verdict.⚠️_deliberately_left_in_place: 11 detector duplicates surviving _dedup_elements and 7 fabricated `.N` primary keys in the KY parser output. Fixing them needs the rejected SCHEMA option (a prompt rule that a page banner is not an element's age_band), which moves code_version_hash and forces a re-record of Tasks 1-4. Deferred on purpose, not overlooked.

rejected.GOLDEN: would set 44 KY elements to the banner value — contradicts the other five states, and would not fix the duplicates since the run also emits null for 24 elements in the same window.
rejected.SCHEMA: the principled fix and the strongest §6 finding, but it moves code_version_hash and forces a re-record of Tasks 1-4. Out of scope for this arXiv round.
